extracted.intended_audience: early-career and mid-career academic mathematicians (assistant/associate professors, new hires, postdocs considering academia)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, actionable guidance for beginning and mid-career mathematicians on succeeding in academic life: teaching, research, service, departmental roles, tenure, and career management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three components for academic evaluation (teaching, research, service)
rubrics_metrics.description: The three big vectors in an academic life are teaching, research, and service; an academic is judged on each in different ways (Tenure Document frames expectations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance these three vectors deliberately: excellence in one can compensate to some extent in others (e.g., major research achievement compensates for weaker service), but tenure decisions examine all three. Consult your institution's Tenure Document to learn how weightings and procedures work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collegiality / departmental fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Collegiality and whether 'you will fit in' matter for long-term success; departments consider whether they'd want you around for decades.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate good relationships with staff, senior faculty, and peers; attend seminars/social events; participate in informal networks. Anti-pattern: hiding in your office and avoiding departmental life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching quality and reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: Teaching is a visible, important component: prepare lectures carefully, write a good syllabus, choose readable texts, design and grade exams fairly, and be courteous and professional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teaching skill is cultivated—seek mentors, read teaching guides (e.g., KRA1), solicit peer feedback, and avoid over-investing in teaching to the exclusion of research. Good teaching reputation is a plus in tenure review, though rarely sufficient alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation and presentation of lectures
rubrics_metrics.description: Convey the impression you are a professional who is on top of the material and who knows how to communicate it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare lectures carefully, pitch material to student level, encourage participation. Professional demeanor and clarity can offset other shortcomings; practice and continual refinement improve effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exam design and fair grading
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing good exams, grading them fairly, and correctly assigning course grades are essential pedagogical skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop insight into assessment; consult experienced colleagues; create clear rubrics; handle exceptional student situations with calm, flexible solutions rather than punitive responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching evaluations (student feedback)
rubrics_metrics.description: Teaching evaluations are routinely collected (often at semester end) and used in personnel decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful of evaluation processes (paper or online), strive for fair treatment and clarity in class policies, and document teaching efforts; use evaluations to improve but know their limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seminar participation and giving talks
rubrics_metrics.description: Join and participate actively in seminars; volunteer to give talks and attend regularly to build visibility and networks in your research area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seminar attendance, presenting, and social engagement (e.g., colloquium lunches) help establish research identity and collegial ties; missing informal gatherings can reduce visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developing a research program
rubrics_metrics.description: Find problems worth working on, solve them, write them up, and publish; develop an identifiable research trajectory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn how to choose problems, balance depth vs. publishability, work alone and in collaboration strategically, and continuously refine your research agenda (see Chapter 4 topics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing a research reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: Research reputation is built via publishing, conference presence, collaborations, grants, and prizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish consistently, present at conferences, visit institutes, seek external recognition and awards, and cultivate productive collaborations; reputation can offset weaker elements elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing papers: writing and submission process
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishing involves writing clear papers, submitting to appropriate journals, undergoing refereeing, and responding to revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write lucid exposition (see A Primer of Mathematical Writing), choose suitable journals, respond professionally to referees, and keep a steady output of quality work rather than sporadic pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing books and expository work
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing textbooks, survey articles, and expository pieces is a respected form of professional contribution and part of exposition duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books take major time investments; plan audience and scope carefully; expository writing raises visibility and service to the profession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applying for and managing grants
rubrics_metrics.description: How to apply for a grant (e.g., NSF) and act as a Principal Investigator to secure research funding (soft money).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn grant-writing skills, manage budgets and reporting, and be aware that soft-money is not permanent—use grants to support research activity strategically and sustainably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentorship (finding and being a mentor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify a senior faculty mentor for reality checks and career guidance; later, serve as a mentor yourself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek mentors via seminars, teas, and social events; cultivate an authentic relationship rather than accepting artificial assignments; mentor students and junior colleagues responsibly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Networking and professional societies
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with organizations (e.g., Project NExT, YMN, AMS, MAA, SIAM) to network, learn about publishing, tenure, and teaching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participate in meetings, join discussion groups, and leverage society programs for career development and peer support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and committee work
rubrics_metrics.description: Service (departmental and university committees, task forces) will be assigned and figures into tenure and promotion decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform service responsibly, but be selective about major administrative commitments (vice-chair, chair). Document service in your dossier and weigh time cost against research goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental citizenship
rubrics_metrics.description: Being a good departmental citizen includes mentoring, advising, attending meetings, and contributing to curricula and departmental life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage in activities that hold the department together, work well with staff, and support colleagues—these intangibles influence tenure and long-term standing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graduate advising and directing theses
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct Ph.D. theses responsibly: chair thesis committees, guide research, and prepare students for the profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supervising graduate students is a major service and scholarly role—set expectations early, provide constructive feedback, and manage committee interactions professionally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undergraduate advising and curriculum oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Manage undergraduate programs, advise majors, and contribute to curriculum development (Vice-Chair roles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance program needs with departmental resources; be thoughtful about textbook choices and course design; document curricular contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choosing textbooks and course materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Select appropriate, readable texts for courses that match student level and course goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider pedagogy, accessibility, available supplements, and alignment with departmental curriculum; discuss choices with colleagues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using media and technology in teaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate use of media (projectors, online resources) can enhance teaching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt technology judiciously; ensure it serves pedagogy rather than distracts; seek training and colleague advice when adopting new tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative vs. independent research
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide when to work on your own and when to collaborate; both modes have distinct advantages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborate to broaden perspective and productivity; maintain clear authorship and contribution expectations; balance solo work to build individual identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Being a referee and editorial interactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Refereeing and dealing with editors are professional duties; editors have distinct purposes and types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referee promptly and constructively; respond professionally to editors; learn editorial norms and maintain collegial tone in publication exchanges.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to give talks effectively
rubrics_metrics.description: Giving talks (colloquia, seminars, conference talks) is key to communication and reputation-building.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare for audience and venue, structure talks clearly, use visuals appropriately, and practice timing; resources and checklists are available (e.g., referenced giving-a-talk handouts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling sticky situations: conflict resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice for dealing with problem colleagues, problematic graduate students, inability to get along, legal issues, and the two-body problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek mediation, document issues, consult mentors and administration, be pragmatic about career moves, and prioritize long-term professional health over transient disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career alternatives and industry positions
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-academic career paths exist (industry, government labs); these roles have different expectations (seminars, mentoring) and rewards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand what industry roles entail, consider them as viable options, and realize skills transfer (problem solving, mentoring, presentations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sabbatical leaves and professional travel
rubrics_metrics.description: Sabbaticals (typically every seven years) and travel to institutes/conferences support research growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan sabbaticals to advance research, collaborate, or refresh; use professional travel to build networks and visibility—budget and approval processes vary by institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenure dossier and Tenure Document procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The tenure dossier compiles teaching evaluations, outside review letters, publication lists, service records; tenure decisions follow the institution's Tenure Document and tenure clock.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble a clear, comprehensive dossier; understand timelines and what evidence is valued; seek external letters from recognized peers; document all contributions carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department Chair responsibilities and management
rubrics_metrics.description: Chair duties include budget management, promotion & tenure oversight, hiring, faculty development, reward system, interface with dean, raising money, and handling discipline and complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If considering chairship, assess time commitment and potential impact on research; exercise 'first, do no harm' leadership; learn personnel and budgetary skills; delegate and support faculty activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time management and work-life balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Manage time across teaching, research, service, family, and personal life; strike a sustainable balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize tasks, set boundaries (know when you are done for the day), delegate when appropriate, and maintain health and relationships to sustain a long career.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion beyond tenure and career progression
rubrics_metrics.description: Promotion through academic ranks and post-tenure career choices require continued productivity and service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep teaching alive, maintain research agenda, document achievements for promotions, and consider roles (administration, prizes, national service) that align with goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition: prizes, encomia, and professional honors
rubrics_metrics.description: Prizes and honors (e.g., Steele, Veblen, Satter, Sloan) recognize excellence and raise profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue opportunities that increase visibility (high-quality research, expository work, national service); nominations often require peers—cultivate networks.
